quoted_tweet.author: Glenn Williams
quoted_tweet.text:
A fruit fly brain built a guitar.

Google and Janelia released the full wiring of a fly brain last week. 166,700 neurons, 25 million connections. I loaded all of it, gave it eyes, and put a light in front of it. Wherever it walked, it laid a block. The light traced a guitar. The fly did the rest.

The wiring is real. The dynamics, the eyes, and the joystick are mine. Every loop in the trail is the fly losing the light and hunting for it. It finished in 18 seconds of brain time.

12 years building guitars. This is the worst one I've ever made and I can't stop watching it.

This is round one. I'm going to keep refining it and see how far "fly builds guitar" can go.

I assign essentially 0% probability that Anthropic or OpenAI will slow down frontier development in any meaningful way. 

And that majority of the "regulation" they try making is regulatory capture to slow down competition. 

1. Anthropic/OpenAI will not willingly hand over their lead to Gemini, xAI, Meta, or another frontier lab.

-> Elon will want a slowdown to catch up with OpenAI. 
-> OpenAI will want a regulatory framework to slow down xAI + competition. 

Every lab has an incentive to support rules that constrain competitors more than they constrain itself

2. The US is not going to meaningfully slow frontier AI development while China continues advancing. (as seen with Trump's post today about rejecting AI slowdown). 

It would be probably the most flagrant national security risk if China leapfrogged the US in capability. 

Especially when both sides have called frontier AI capabilities "cyber nuclear weapons" 

3. China will not slow down frontier AI development. That is a given. 

It will be theater if any of these parties agrees so publicly, because behind the scenes:

-> They'll likely keep on progressing, whether it's OpenAI, the US Government, or China. 

If they wanted to slow down, they could have done so themselves at any point in time: 

Yet everyone is still fighting over the scarce resources to run AI as seen with memory procurement from Samsung going all the way to 2031. 

Or the $NVDA / $AVGO supply constrained 70-100%+ Y/Y growth protections.

So I suggest people unfollow the clowns on X that predict AI stocks from $NVDA to $TSM to $MU will crash for engagement. 

All this does is cause retail to panic short term and hand over the keys to the kingdom over to others.

Be Anthropic:

Call for: “limiting the ingredients that go into frontier models, such as training compute”

> secure $517 Billion in compute deals over last 11 months

Proclaim: “We have tried to prioritize caution over speed and prudence over profit.”

> actively speedrun NASDAQ IPO in October while others like OpenAI delayed theirs to 2027

Suggest: “employee-like access to a team of embedded third-party evaluators” for regulatory oversight of frontier labs

> after becoming one of the two leaders…

I cannot emphasize enough how much GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1 are already enough for transformative impact in large sections of the economy. They can reliably do weeks worth of human work when properly guided & harnessed.

Those effects will not be all at once and be uneven, but the fact that change will occur is inevitable no matter how the frontier is paced. But inevitable change does not mean the type of change is inevitable. It is increasingly important that we develop & share models of AI-human work that enhance, rather than only replace, human labor. The labs have a role to play in doing this, but so do companies and industries experimenting with AI adoption, as well as policy makers who can incentivize this sort of inplemenation.

This work is important regardless of existential risk, and needs a lot more focus.

I wrote about one set of approaches to the problem (The Twilight Factory), but there are others. Yes, it is likely that some automation and replacement is inevitable, but that doesn't mean that we need to default to automation as the default solution. https://www.oneusefulthing.org/p/agency-and-agents

免费、优雅的 Markdown 编辑器 ColaMD 
今天正式发布 2.1 版本
新版本支持了标签页，可以方便地在同一个窗口里浏览多个文件

- 创建标签页，⌘T
- 关闭标签页，⌘W
- 在文件列表中⌘+鼠标点击，可迅速打开多个标签

这个版本还优化了安装包的体积，从 200 多 M 到现在 80M，瘦身 60%。
社区用户评价，这个版本的完成度已经相当高了，就算养老都没问题，可以供大众用户稳定使用，推荐所有用户前来体验。

这个版本也将作为一个阶段性的终点
后续我们将构建开放的插件系统，把分栏、AI、工作区 等功能作为插件引入，让每个人定制自己的 Markdown 编辑器，同时不影响核心功能的稳定性

ColaMD 现已支持 Mac Windows Linux
开源仓库 https://github.com/marswaveai/ColaMD
永久官网 http://ColaMD.com
